rows.host_support: 2 full-featured USB-C laptop inputs; Windows uses DP MST; macOS is supported but not for dual independent MST desktops.
rows.display_capability: Windows: 2 × 4K @ 60Hz. macOS: two outputs can light but mirror rather than extend independently.
rows.switching_method: Panel button; wired remote switch button supported.
rows.keyboard_mouse_channel: Shared keyboard/mouse through USB; directly paired Bluetooth input does not automatically follow KVM switching.
rows.clamshell_support: Yes; AV Access explicitly lists clamshell support.
rows.power_delivery: 60W USB-C charging per connected laptop; both hosts remain powered.
rows.known_non_working_combinations: macOS cannot create two independent extended displays through the C20 MST path; the two monitors also cannot be split one-per-host while USB peripherals are shared.
rows.official_support_evidence: AV Access troubleshooting says MacBook dual displays through this MST path are mirrored rather than independently extended. It also says a 4K display falling to 1080p can depend on the laptop's simultaneous video-stream capability and the monitor port, and recommends lowering resolution/refresh rate when video fails. Source

rows.host_support: USB-C host connection carries DisplayPort video and data; HDMI and DisplayPort inputs are also available.
rows.display_capability: Built-in panel: 1 × 2560 × 1440 @ up to 144Hz; DisplayPort daisy-chain output is supported, with downstream ceiling host-dependent.
rows.display_interfaces: HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4 DSC input/output, USB-C with DisplayPort support.
rows.keyboard_mouse_channel: Keyboard and mouse share through the built-in USB hub when using KVM.
rows.official_support_evidence: ASUS's product FAQ requires one KVM host to use USB-C with DP Alt Mode; a second host using HDMI or DisplayPort also needs a separate USB upstream cable for keyboard/mouse switching. A video-only second-host cable is therefore not enough for KVM control. Source

rows.host_support: 2 USB-C computers; DisplayLink-certified for Windows, macOS and ChromeOS.
rows.display_capability: 2 × 4K @ 60Hz external displays, including extended dual displays on base Apple M-series MacBooks through DisplayLink.
rows.switching_method: Push button; downloadable hot-key software for Windows and macOS.
rows.peripheral_usb_capability: 2 × USB-A + 1 × USB-C at USB 3.2 Gen 2 10Gbps, plus HID USB at 480Mbps.
rows.power_delivery: USB PD 3.0: 90W to active host and 45W to second host; both charge simultaneously.
rows.official_support_evidence: StarTech's DisplayLink support FAQ says macOS 10.15 or later requires DisplayLink Manager plus the required Screen Recording/accessibility permissions; if the app is not running or permissions are disabled, DisplayLink-driven external displays may not appear. Source
rows.public_user_report: On StarTech's official IT Pro Community, a MacBook Pro M3 user reported the second DisplayLink monitor going black when Screen Recording permission was disabled; StarTech support explained that the permission is required for the virtual display path. This is a DisplayLink support case, not a 129N-specific reliability test. Source

rows.host_support: Thunderbolt hosts and USB-C hosts with DisplayPort Alt Mode; Dell lists Windows 10/11, Ubuntu 20.04+ and ChromeOS M107+.
rows.display_capability: 2 × 4K @ 60Hz on qualifying Thunderbolt/HBR3/DSC combinations; up to four external displays under specific bandwidth/topology conditions.
rows.display_interfaces: 2 × DisplayPort 1.4, HDMI 2.0, MFDP USB-C and Thunderbolt 4 USB-C display paths.
rows.switching_method: Not a KVM; single-host dock, so switching hosts requires reconnecting upstream or a separate switching layer.
rows.keyboard_mouse_channel: Standard USB device path; no dedicated KVM keyboard/mouse channel listed.
rows.peripheral_usb_capability: 3 × USB-A USB 3.2 Gen 1; USB-C Gen 2 data plus Thunderbolt 4 ports on compatible hosts.
rows.power_delivery: Up to 130W to supported Dell systems or 90W to non-Dell systems with the 180W adapter.
rows.known_non_working_combinations: Rear HDMI and MFDP USB-C video paths are muxed and cannot both be used as simultaneous video outputs; non-Thunderbolt hosts lose Thunderbolt features.
rows.official_support_evidence: Dell troubleshooting says monitor count and resolution depend on the host graphics path; with Intel graphics plus the system LCD, only two displays may be supported, while discrete Nvidia/AMD configurations can support three external displays plus the system LCD. Dell also recommends a dock power-cycle sequence for flicker or USB failures. Source
rows.public_user_report: A Dell Community WD22TB4 case reports dual-4K HBR2 behavior falling from 60Hz to 30Hz after reconnecting the dock, with connection-order workarounds discussed in the official community thread. Treat this as a user/support case, not a universal WD22TB4 fact. Source

rows.host_support: Thunderbolt 4/3, USB4 and USB-C computers; official minimums include macOS 11.4+ and Windows 10 20H2+.
rows.display_capability: Windows / Intel Mac / ChromeOS: up to 2 × 4K @ 60Hz. M1 Pro/Max: up to 2 × 6K @ 60Hz. Original M1: one external display through Thunderbolt.
rows.display_interfaces: DisplayPort 1.4 plus downstream Thunderbolt 4/USB4 display paths.
rows.switching_method: Not a KVM; single-host dock with no host-switch control listed.
rows.keyboard_mouse_channel: Standard USB path; no dedicated KVM keyboard/mouse channel listed.
rows.peripheral_usb_capability: 5 × USB-A 10Gbps and 3 × USB-C 10Gbps, plus Thunderbolt 4 ports.
rows.known_non_working_combinations: Original M1 Macs do not support dual external displays through TS4; USB-C hosts have reduced functionality and 2.5Gb Ethernet is Thunderbolt-host dependent.
rows.official_support_evidence: CalDigit's TS4 support knowledge base documents shared bandwidth groups: many USB ports share the same 10Gbps USB hub, while DisplayPort and downstream Thunderbolt ports share the same 40Gbps Thunderbolt bandwidth. High-bandwidth peripherals therefore compete within those groups rather than receiving dedicated bandwidth. Source

rows.host_support: USB-C with DisplayPort Alt Mode, USB4 or Thunderbolt; Windows 10/11, macOS 11+ and ChromeOS 100+. Full display capability uses DisplayLink software.
rows.display_capability: Up to 3 × 4K @ 60Hz with a DP 1.4 host path; Display 2 and 3 use DisplayLink at up to 4K @ 60Hz each. DP 1.2 can limit Display 1 to 4K @ 30Hz.
rows.display_interfaces: 3 HDMI/DisplayPort output pairs; choose one connector from each display pair.
rows.switching_method: Not a KVM; single-host dock with no host-switch control listed.
rows.keyboard_mouse_channel: Standard USB path; no dedicated KVM keyboard/mouse channel listed.
rows.power_delivery: Current hardware revision: up to 100W USB-C PD; older units with the same model number may be the earlier 60W revision.
rows.known_non_working_combinations: Plugable does not recommend this DisplayLink dock for Linux, gaming or graphics-heavy work; Lenovo ThinkPad P16 Gen 2 is listed as a currently incompatible/limited host combination.
rows.official_support_evidence: Plugable says Night Light and display color calibration are not supported on the DisplayLink-controlled display pairs, does not recommend this DisplayLink dock for Linux, and lists the Lenovo ThinkPad P16 Gen 2 as an incompatible/limited host because different USB-C/TB ports expose different subsets of display and USB functions. Source
rows.public_user_report: Plugable's official product/support page states that users have reported limited UD-6950PDZ compatibility on the ThinkPad P16 Gen 2 depending on which host port is used. This is vendor-published user-report evidence, not SetupMeld testing. Source

rows.host_support: Requires Thunderbolt 4. Anker lists M1 Pro/Max support and excludes base M1/M2 MacBooks and ASUS laptops with AMD CPUs.
rows.display_capability: Windows supports 2 × 4K @ 60Hz and additional higher-count combinations subject to host limits; macOS topology depends on the Mac chip.
rows.display_interfaces: 1 × HDMI 2.1, 2 × DisplayPort and a downstream Thunderbolt display path.
rows.switching_method: Not a KVM; single-host dock with no host-switch control listed.
rows.keyboard_mouse_channel: Standard USB path; no dedicated KVM keyboard/mouse channel listed.
rows.power_delivery: USB PD 3.0 up to 100W; when both 30W USB-C charging ports are used, Anker states laptop output can fall to 65W.
rows.known_non_working_combinations: Not compatible with base M1/M2 MacBooks or ASUS laptops using AMD CPUs.
rows.official_support_evidence: Anker's exact-model FAQ says the host must support Thunderbolt 4, the dock is not compatible with base M1/M2 MacBooks, and laptop charging can fall from the advertised 100W maximum to 65W when both 30W USB-C charging ports are used. Source

rows.host_support: Thunderbolt 4/3, USB4 and full-function USB-C hosts; Windows 10+ and macOS 11.4+ are listed, with reduced display capability on some hosts.
rows.display_capability: Windows and supported Intel/Pro/Max Macs: up to 2 × 4K @ 60Hz. Base M1/M2/M3 Macs: 1 × 4K @ 60Hz. Full-function USB-C: one display.
rows.display_interfaces: DisplayPort 1.4 plus 2 × downstream Thunderbolt 4 display-capable ports.
rows.switching_method: Not a KVM; single-host dock with no host-switch control listed.
rows.keyboard_mouse_channel: Standard USB path; no dedicated KVM keyboard/mouse channel listed.
rows.peripheral_usb_capability: 1 × USB-C 10Gbps; 2 × USB-A 10Gbps; 2 × USB-A 5Gbps, plus Thunderbolt 4 data ports.
rows.power_delivery: Up to 90W laptop charging from the included 180W power supply.
rows.known_non_working_combinations: Full-function USB-C hosts support only one display; UGREEN also lists the 2018 Intel Mac mini as incompatible.
rows.official_support_evidence: UGREEN's exact-model compatibility notes say full-function USB-C hosts support only one external display, base M1/M2/M3 Macs support a single 4K@60Hz display, Intel Mac mini 2018 is not compatible, and the dock must be connected to power to function. Source
